items.stem: A project's net present value (NPV) is positive when:

options.text: The discounted benefits exceed the discounted costs
options.rationale: Correct: a positive NPV means the project adds value at the chosen discount rate.

options.text: The payback period is longer than the project life
options.rationale: A long payback does not imply positive NPV.

options.text: The initial cost is the largest single cash flow
options.rationale: Cash-flow size alone does not set NPV's sign.

options.text: No discount rate has been applied

items.explanation: Correct: a positive NPV means the project adds value at the chosen discount rate.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO reflect the time value of money? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Money available now can be invested to earn a return
options.rationale: Correct: earning potential makes present money worth more.

options.text: Future cash flows must be discounted to compare with present ones
options.rationale: Correct: discounting puts cash flows on a common time basis.

options.text: A dollar in ten years is worth more than a dollar today
options.rationale: Future dollars are worth less, not more, today.

options.text: Interest rates are irrelevant to project choice
options.rationale: Interest rates are central to economic comparison.

items.explanation: Correct: earning potential makes present money worth more.

items.stem: In cash-flow analysis, depreciation is best treated as:

options.text: A non-cash expense that affects taxes, not a direct cash outflow
options.rationale: Correct: depreciation is non-cash but reduces taxable income.

options.text: A cash payment made each year
options.rationale: Depreciation is not a cash outflow.

options.text: The salvage value of the asset
options.rationale: Salvage is a separate cash flow at disposal.
Depreciation matters through its tax effect.

items.explanation: Correct: depreciation is non-cash but reduces taxable income.
